title: Beyond the statistics: the people and communities affected by the Nepal flash floods and landslide - British Red Cross
description: Beyond the statistics: the people and communities affected by the Nepal flash floods and landslide  British Red Cross
publisher.title: British Red Cross
full_article:
Meeting Nepal on its own terms

As the car climbed higher, we saw a snapshot of rural life in Nepal. So many things stood out for me, like a little girl running up and down the steep hillsides in flip-flops.

Syabrubesi was lined with three- or four-storey hotels, many with wooden or brick gables and coffee shops on the ground floor, with a main road cutting through the valley next to the Bhote Koshi river. Its water flowed quickly with white waves and a low roar.

Our hotel seemed to be run by a woman who wore traditional Nepali clothes and had a group of young men to help. It was clear that someone had put in a lot of time and effort to make the building welcoming and weatherproof, essential for the harsh Nepali winters and monsoons.

Outside, there were many young men on motorbikes and other travellers on the same route. Later there seemed to be a party with people sounding cheerful and relaxed through our open window.

People from my tour group walked down the road to look at and listen to the river. It was high, since it’s Nepal’s rainy season, but it didn’t yet look like the killer it would become.
translated:
अपन शर्त पर नेपाल सँ भेंट करब

गाड़ी जहिना-जहिना ऊँच चढ़ैत गेल तहिना नेपालक ग्रामीण जीवनक झलक देखलहुँ । हमरा लेल एतेक रास बात ठाढ़ छल, जेना कोनो छोट बच्ची फ्लिप-फ्लॉप मे खड़ा पहाड़ी ढाल पर ऊपर-नीचा दौड़ैत हो।

स्याब्रुबेसी मे तीन-चारि मंजिला होटल सबहक लाइन लागल छलैक, जाहि मे कतेको मे लकड़ीक वा ईंटाक गेबल आ भूतल पर कॉफी शॉप छलैक, भोटे कोशी नदीक बगल मे घाटी केँ काटि क' एकटा मुख्य सड़क छलैक. एकर पानि उज्जर लहरि आ कम गर्जनसँ तेजीसँ बहैत छल ।

हमरा लोकनिक होटल जेना कोनो महिला द्वारा संचालित छल जे पारंपरिक नेपाली वस्त्र पहिरने छलीह आ मददि करय लेल युवकक समूह छल. ई स्पष्ट छल जे नेपाली कठोर जाड़ आ मानसून के लेल आवश्यक भवन के स्वागत योग्य आ मौसम के प्रतिरोधी बनेबा में कियो बहुत समय आ मेहनत केने छल ।

बाहर मोटरसाइकिल पर सवार बहुत रास युवक आ ओही रस्ता पर आन यात्री सब छल। बाद मे जेना कोनो पार्टी भेल छल जाहि मे हमरा लोकनिक खुजल खिड़की सँ लोक सभ हँसमुख आ आराम सँ आवाज दैत छल ।

हमर टूर ग्रुप के लोक सब नदी के देखय आ सुनय लेल सड़क पर चलैत छल. ऊँच छल, किएक त’ नेपाल’क बरसात’क मौसम छैक, मुदा एखन धरि ओ हत्यारा नहि बुझाइत छलैक जे ई बनि जायत.

title: Japan to dispatch team of experts to flood-hit Nepal - Japan Wire by Kyodo News
description: Japan to dispatch team of experts to flood-hit Nepal  Japan Wire by Kyodo News
publisher.title: Japan Wire by Kyodo News
full_article:
The seven-member team will arrive in Nepal on Friday. More than 1,200 people have been killed and around 5,500 remain missing following the Aug. 26 disaster, with five Japanese nationals among those unaccounted for, according to the ministry.

"Nepal has been a longtime friend of Japan, and our government will not hesitate to provide all sorts of support," Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi told reporters in Ulaanbaatar.

The team will consist of officials from the ministry, the National Police Agency, the Metropolitan Police Department, and the Japan International Cooperation Agency, the ministry said.

Motegi also said a separate team from JICA was already operating in Nepal on Wednesday to assess medical needs.

सात सदस्यीय टीम शुक्रदिन नेपाल पहुंचत। मंत्रालय के अनुसार 26 अगस्त के आपदा के बाद 1200 सं बेसी लोक के मौत भ गेल अछि आओर करीब 5500 लोक लापता अछि, जाहि मे पांच जापानी नागरिक के कोनो हिसाब नहिं.

जापान केरऽ विदेश मंत्री तोशिमित्सु मोटेगी न॑ उलानबातर म॑ पत्रकारऽ स॑ बातचीत म॑ कहलकै कि नेपाल जापान केरऽ बहुत दिन स॑ दोस्त रहलऽ छै, आरू हमरऽ सरकार हर तरह के सहयोग दै म॑ संकोच नै करतै ।

मन्त्रालय जनौलक अछि जे टीममे मंत्रालय, राष्ट्रिय प्रहरी एजेंसी, महानगरीय पुलिस विभाग, आ जापान अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सहयोग एजेंसीके अधिकारी रहत ।

मोटेगी इहो कहलनि जे, बुधदिन नेपाल मे जाइका सं अलग टीम पहिने सं चिकित्सा के जरूरत के आकलन करय लेल संचालित अछि.

title: Climate injustices have been laid bare in the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster | Letters - The Guardian
description: Climate injustices have been laid bare in the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster | Letters  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
The recent glacial collapse and catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet are not isolated tragedies (Report, 28 August). They reflect accelerating climate disruption that disproportionately affects the countries and people that are least responsible for global emissions.

As climate change intensifies, glaciers around the world, including in the Himalayas, are melting at unprecedented rates, destabilising ecosystems and causing glacial collapse and ice-and-rock landslides, destroying settlements, villages and livelihoods in minutes. No one died when a Swiss glacier collapsed last year, owing to early-warning systems that were in place. But a lack of early-warning systems means that the disaster in Nepal and Tibet has led to hundreds of deaths and thousands missing.

Events like these are not “natural disasters”. They are due to global warming and climate injustices, and also flawed development policies, including rampant property developments on vulnerable floodplains. They call for better disaster preparedness and investment in early-warning systems. Most importantly, they require global action.

The UK has long positioned itself as a leader in international development and climate action. Yet recent UK commitments have fallen far short of what is required – including the decision to raid the diminished aid budget to switch international climate finance grants to loans, to fund a bus-fare cap.

The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, recently spoke compellingly about the need to put the climate crisis and overseas development at the heart of UK international relations. These words must now translate into action. The UK must step up its development commitments and funding for climate adaptation, and loss and damage, to support those living on the frontlines of climate change.

The recent glacial floods remind us that climate disruption is global, and highly unequal. The UK must act urgently. Anything less is a failure of responsibility.

Prof Lyla Mehta

Institute of Development Studies

Sunil Acharya is correct when he states: “The countries that benefited most from fossil fuel-driven growth have a responsibility to cut emissions rapidly” (Nepal-Tibet flood: this is the cost of not acting in the face of the climate crisis, 28 August).

This was the founding principle of the global “contraction and convergence” framework, tabled by India, China and the African Group of Nations in Kyoto at Cop3 in 1997.

Had we enacted this, we would now be on a safe, and equitable, 30-year contraction path, avoiding the worst of the climate crisis and ensuring our survival. Instead, we remain adrift, with no viable solution or plan. Is it really too late to adopt this framework?

Lynda McDonald

Portaferry, County Down

The key question is: who should pay for this disaster? Yes, the rich world should pay, but the bills should be sent to all the fossil-fuel companies that have known this risk for at least half a century and have ignored it. If they refuse to pay, all of us in countries that have profited from the fossil-driven benefits of “progress” should, through our governments, pay a progressive tax on all things based on fossil fuels, to cover the past, present and future costs of climate change.

Jan Bengtsson

Uppsala, Sweden
translated:
नेपाल आरू तिब्बत म॑ हाल केरऽ हिमनदी पतन आरू विनाशकारी बाढ़ अलग-थलग त्रासदी नै छै (रिपोर्ट, २८ अगस्त) । इ जलवायु मे तेजी सं गड़बड़ी कें दर्शाबै छै जे गैर-आनुपातिक रूप सं ओय देशक आ लोगक कें प्रभावित करय छै जे वैश्विक उत्सर्जन कें लेल कम जिम्मेदार छै.

जलवायु परिवर्तन तेज होय के साथ-साथ हिमालय सहित दुनिया भर के ग्लेशियर अभूतपूर्व दर स॑ पिघली रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र अस्थिर होय रहलऽ छै आरू हिमनदी केरऽ पतन आरू बर्फ-चट्टान के भूस्खलन होय ​​रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ मिनटऽ म॑ बस्ती, गाँव आरू रोजी-रोटी नष्ट होय रहलऽ छै । पिछला साल स्विस ग्लेशियर गिरला पर ककरो मौत नहि भेल छल, जेकर कारण छल पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली जे लागू छल । लेकिन पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली के अभाव के मतलब छै कि नेपाल आरू तिब्बत के आपदा के कारण सैकड़ों लोगऽ के मौत आरू हजारों लोगऽ के लापता होय गेलऽ छै ।

एहि तरहक घटना “प्राकृतिक आपदा” नहि होइत छैक | ई ग्लोबल वार्मिंग आरू जलवायु अन्याय के कारण छै, आरू साथ ही साथ त्रुटिपूर्ण विकास नीतियऽ के कारण छै, जेकरा म॑ कमजोर बाढ़ के मैदानऽ प॑ बेतहाशा संपत्ति विकास भी शामिल छै । ओ सब आपदा के लेल बेहतर तैयारी आ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली में निवेश के आह्वान करैत छथि। सबस पैघ गप इ जे एहि लेल वैश्विक कार्रवाई क जरूरत अछि।

ब्रिटेन बहुत दिन स॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय विकास आरू जलवायु कार्रवाई म॑ खुद क॑ अग्रणी के रूप म॑ खड़ा करी चुकलऽ छै । तइयो हाल केरऽ यूके केरऽ प्रतिबद्धता जेतना कम छै, ओकरा स॑ बहुत कम होय गेलऽ छै – जेकरा म॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय जलवायु वित्त अनुदान क॑ ऋण म॑ बदलै लेली, बस-भाड़ा केरऽ सीमा क॑ फंडिंग करै लेली, कम होय गेलऽ सहायता बजट प॑ छापा मारै के फैसला भी शामिल छै ।

विदेश सचिव एड मिलिबैंड न॑ हाल ही म॑ जलवायु संकट आरू विदेशी विकास क॑ यूके केरऽ अंतरराष्ट्रीय संबंधऽ के केंद्र म॑ रखै के जरूरत के बारे म॑ मजबूर करै वाला बात करलकै । ई शब्द आब काज मे बदलय पड़त। जलवायु परिवर्तन कें मोर्चा पर रहय वाला लोगक कें सहायता कें लेल यूके कें जलवायु अनुकूलन, आ नुकसान आ नुकसान कें लेल अपन विकास प्रतिबद्धता आ वित्तपोषण कें तेज करनाय होयत छै.

हाल केरऽ हिमनदी बाढ़ हमरा सब क॑ याद दिलाबै छै कि जलवायु केरऽ व्यवधान वैश्विक छै, आरू बहुत असमान छै । ब्रिटेन के तत्काल कार्रवाई करय पड़त. कम किछुओ जिम्मेदारी के असफलता अछि।

प्रो लाइला मेहता

विकास अध्ययन संस्थान

सुनील आचार्य सही कहै छै: “जीवाश्म ईंधन संचालित विकास स॑ जे देशऽ क॑ सबसें जादा फायदा मिललै, ओकरऽ जिम्मेदारी छै कि उत्सर्जन म॑ तेजी स॑ कटौती करलऽ जाय” (नेपाल-तिब्बत केरऽ बाढ़: जलवायु संकट के सामना म॑ काम नै करै के ई लागत छै, २८ अगस्त) ।

ई वैश्विक “संकुचन आरू अभिसरण” ढाँचा केरऽ संस्थापक सिद्धांत छेलै, जेकरा भारत, चीन आरू क्योटो म॑ अफ्रीकी राष्ट्र समूह न॑ १९९७ म॑ Cop3 म॑ पेश करलकै ।

जं हम सब ई कानून बनौने रहितहुं तं आब हम सब जलवायु संकट सं सब सं खराब सं बचैत आ अपन अस्तित्व सुनिश्चित करैत 30 सालक सुरक्षित, आ न्यायसंगत, संकुचन मार्ग पर रहितहुं. बल्कि हम सब बहैत रहैत छी, कोनो व्यवहार्य समाधान आ योजना नहि। की सच मे एहि ढाँचा के अपनाबय मे बहुत देर भ गेल अछि?

लिंडा मैकडोनाल्ड

पोर्टफेरी, काउंटी डाउन

Dhan ⁠Bahadur Tamang was at ​work in a hydropower project near Nepal's border with China when he sensed a sudden air pressure change in the underground tunnel at ​the Upper Trishuli 1 Hydropower Project.

Under the industrial floodlights, dust started to rise, the 32-year-old recalled: "Something was coming."

Nobody in the tunnel was prepared for what was about to hit them: a flood wave that had by then already flattened entire settlements upstream on the Trishuli ​river and ‌was rolling down the valley with immense destructive power that killed more than 1,252 people in Nepal.

Tamang, ⁠who had been hired by the project as a support worker, said hundreds may have been on site when the disaster struck last week.

"Suddenly, people started running, shouting, ‌and scrambling," Tamang said. "By the time I could have realised anything, I was over a top of a ⁠tanker (truck)."

"Once I was up, the vehicle began moving," he said. Water began rushing into his section of the tunnel. "I felt again and again that I was going to die."

Clinging on to pipes

Tamang was among the lucky ones who escaped. From the top of the truck in the tunnel, he tried to hold on to anything he ​could grab, climbing on pipes and trying to keep his head above the raging water. He ‌suffered injuries to one of his legs.

"My mind kept going to my family. I thought about home, about my mother and father, about the people I might never see again. I shouted, I cried," he said.

When the velocity of flood water receded, Tamang was still alive. So ‌were others, he noticed with relief.

They tried to make their way back to the entrance of the tunnel, but found the route blocked by debris. The only other option was ​to head deeper into the tunnel system.

"As we moved, we started seeing bodies," he said. Some people were injured and unable to move.

"There were bodies all around. We were trying to get out and save our lives. Some were crushed ​so badly that there was no help possible. They were dead bodies," he said.

Not going back to work inside tunnels again

By that ​point the tunnel was in near-complete darkness, so Tamang and the others held hands ​so as to not lose each other as they picked their way through the debris, guided by a single flashlight.

"It was a long, exhausting fight through darkness, water, wreckage, and bodies," he ​said.

Then, he recalled, there was a burst of light. "When we finally came out, the outside brightness felt unreal."

The shaking group of survivors was soon surrounded by other people, who supplied dry clothes. But Tamang said rescue operations proceeded only slowly, as fog stalled helicopter operations.

Determined to return to his family, Tamang made his way with the help of villagers but was later transferred to a hotel and then ⁠to a hospital for a medical checkup.

"When I finally met my wife, she cried," said Tamang, who has had nightmares since his return, with his ⁠mind going back to scenes ​from the tunnel and memories of dead former colleagues.

"I will not work inside hydropower tunnels again," he said. "I do not want to test fate."

title: California attorney petitions State Department for better flood victim identification in Nepal - ABC 10News San Diego
description: California attorney petitions State Department for better flood victim identification in Nepal  ABC 10News San Diego
publisher.title: ABC 10News San Diego
full_article:
A California attorney is calling on the U.S. State Department to do more to identify victims of the Nepal-Tibet floods — a push that began after her nephew and his wife went missing in the disaster.

The San Diego-based couple had been headed to a holy mountain for a sacred Hindu tradition and were expected to be there for a couple of weeks. The family believes they were at the Indo-Tibet border crossing when the floods occurred.

The attorney, Anu Peshawaria, said her nephew's disappearance made the crisis deeply personal.

"My nephew was very dear to me; I brought him up like my own son. To see that happen to my child is very nerve-wracking," Peshawaria said. "His wife, Alka, she was brilliant."

Peshawaria has since joined other families of missing U.S. citizens in circulating a petition directed at Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The petition reads, in part: "Families of missing U.S. citizens of other countries have come together to petition U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio for increased search and rescue assistance and stronger support for the families."

Peshawaria said the effort extends well beyond her own family's situation. Her focus, specifically, is on the identification of bodies recovered from the disaster.

"Thousands of lives have been lost, but we don't see any help forthcoming," Peshawaria said.

Aid organizations are operating in the affected region. The State Department has agreed to an interview about its efforts to help and also promised a statement regarding the petition specifically, but had not responded as of the time of publication.

title: Survivors of Nepal floods speak from the recovery zone - ABC 10News San Diego

full_article:
A landslide and catastrophic flash flood struck Nepal on Wednesday, killing 350 people and leaving 1,300 others missing. Both numbers are expected to grow.

CNN reports a glacial collapse and a landslide caused the flooding along a river that flows from China through Nepal to India. Google Maps identifies that river as the Trishuli River.

When I was 15 — 10 years ago — my family packed our bags and moved to Nepal to help combat human trafficking. While I haven't been to the villages and cities impacted by this disaster, I know people who are in the affected zones.

Paul and Shanti Lama are close friends with family in the impacted zone. They traveled as soon as they heard the news to support their family.

"People lost their shelters, people don't know where they're going to eat, you know? There's no food, no water, no electricity," Paul said.

Paul was able to call with me because he had a solar charging device and can get cell service when standing on the roofs of the buildings that remain standing. Other times, the service is spotty. They and their family are safe, but Paul emphasized the urgent need for help. Nepali people typically buy their drinking water from corner stores, many of which have been wiped out, Paul said.

"Many of my neighbors are missing family members," Paul said. "The first thing we can do is relief work... they're missing all [of their houses] and all of their belongings.. Right away [we need] some food, water and shelter. Basic needs."

The Red Cross, World Central Kitchen, Global Giving, and UNICEF are among the organizations mobilizing to help Nepal, and all are accepting donations.

title: Thousands dead or missing after Nepal disaster; Oregonians seek ways to help - KATU
description: Thousands dead or missing after Nepal disaster; Oregonians seek ways to help  KATU
publisher.title: KATU
full_article:
PORTLAND, Ore. (KATU) — The tragedy in Nepal has killed more than 1,252 people, while more than 4,000 others remain missing. About 90 of those missing people are Americans. It has devastated towns and villages, leaving tens of thousands of people displaced.

Images show homes demolished by water and people pulled from the mud. It is one of the worst tragedies the country has ever seen.

With many people still missing, Oregonians are feeling the emotional pain. Bindu KC, vice president of the Nepali Association of Oregon, said it is difficult to see the devastation on television.

“It’s shocking. It’s really difficult to express the emotions in words. Many of the Nepalese in the United States and all over the world, I’m sure, have spent sleepless nights,” KC said.

READ MORE | Death toll tops 1,000 in Nepal floods as 80 Americans remain missing

It is especially painful, she said, because she knows people dealing with unbearable loss.

“One of my family friends, my brother’s friend, have been directly affected. They found their body in the mud. It’s hard to express that.”

For those who survived, many lost everything.

“Their houses, the place they call their hometown, their community, their villages, their schools, all their livelihoods have been now washed away. They have nothing. So I can, the pain is unbearable. I can, it’s beyond the imagination, I would say,” KC said.

The Nepalese community can use all the help it can get right now.

“I think they are waiting for us, people like us, for sending help, sending our support to them, emotional support, our kindness, compassion. And the real physical help they need currently, they are out of food, they do not have shelter, they have no drinking water, nothing,” KC said.

Many countries, including the United States, are stepping in to help. Even though rebuilding will take time, KC said it is important for the community to support one another.

“One message I would like to say to all community is falling of mountain was not in our hand, but what’s in our hand is we can choose how to lift each other out of the mud, how we can express our kindness, how can we be compassionate, and then we can support each other to heal the survivors, to heal the people who have been directly affected by this disaster.”

She urged people to donate to relief organizations, saying every dollar counts and can make a difference.

People can donate through the Nepali Association of Oregon.

title: More than 11,000 rescued in Nepal floods as desperate search for survivors continues - Scripps News
description: More than 11,000 rescued in Nepal floods as desperate search for survivors continues  Scripps News
publisher.title: Scripps News
full_article:
A week after catastrophic flash floods struck the Nepal-China border region, more than 11,000 people have been rescued, but thousands remain missing or unaccounted for as search operations continue.

Officials say they are not giving up, and rescue efforts remain active on the ground. Many families, however, say they are losing hope of finding their loved ones and have begun using effigies and photographs to put missing family members to rest.

RELATED STORY | Missing tourists in Nepal floods make contact as death toll tops 1,100

Others say they are still hoping for a miracle — including families of 900 workers believed to be trapped inside hydropower tunnels in Nepal. Rescue teams and foreign specialist crews have been working for days to clear the tunnels of thick mud. It remains unclear how many of the trapped workers are still alive.

Nepal's government has called last week's flood a catastrophic Himalayan tsunami, saying the country has not seen anything like it in recent memory.

A new alert has been issued in some of the hardest-hit areas. Officials warn that with more rain in the forecast, rivers could overflow and trigger additional flash flooding. Many residents returning to their villages and towns say nothing remains of their former lives.

IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Nepal warns of possible fresh flooding as communities grapple with devastation

Authorities estimate around 20,000 houses will need to be rebuilt in safer locations, as Nepal faces a massive recovery and rebuilding effort in one of the world's poorest countries.

full_article:
Dear All Hands & Hearts Family,

This week, I kissed my boys, Lukas (12) and Frans (9), goodbye and sent them off to school.

After a long summer, there is something almost restorative about watching your children leave again: the backpacks, the lunchboxes, the excitement over new books, and the slight nervousness about the teacher they will meet, and whether the older children were right after all.

Just last week, however, the world was watching Nepal.

Devastating flash floods swept through communities, destroying homes and taking lives. For days, helicopters moved in and out in an increasingly desperate search for those still missing. The chances of finding people alive became smaller by the hour, but the hope did not disappear.

For the All Hands & Hearts family, Nepal is not somewhere we simply respond to. It is somewhere we belong. We have been working in Nepal for more than a decade. We first arrived after the 2015 earthquakes and, together with our Nepali team, went on to build schools across the country, including in Nuwakot. So when the floods came, we knew where to go. Our school communities are safe and accounted for. Gambhir, Pradeep and Rupa, now joined by international staff, have been working day and night to help stabilize the most basic human needs: food, clean water, shelter, generators, PPE, hygiene and children’s kits.

In the days ahead, we are strengthening displacement centers with showers, bathrooms and handwashing stations. This is the work we know. We are good at building. It is simply who we are.



But as we move through the communities, we are also seeing what comes next.

Schools have been heavily damaged. Others are being used as temporary shelters by families who have lost their homes. And this is where the immediate response becomes something longer-term.

 Dhauleshwori School – Chaku, Sindhupalchok District, Nepal

Help Us Rebuild 20 Schools in Nepal

Schools sit at the heart of a community. They are places for children to learn, but they are also part of the infrastructure that allows a community to recover. When children have a safe place to return to, parents have more freedom to rebuild their homes, restore their livelihoods and begin putting their lives back together.

That is why we are making a commitment: 20 schools. Two years. $5 million.

Over the next two years, we aim to raise $5 million to rebuild 20 schools in the communities that need them most.



We already have a match for the first $300,000 in donations as part of our Back to School Campaign. Will you join us?

With so much gratitude, Nicolette Koeman

Chief Engagement Officer

title: Should You Travel to Nepal Right Now? What Locals Want International Travelers to Know - Condé Nast Traveler
description: Should You Travel to Nepal Right Now? What Locals Want International Travelers to Know  Condé Nast Traveler
publisher.title: Condé Nast Traveler
full_article:
I arrive in Kathmandu on the last day of August, just five days after devastating flash floods—caused by a glacier and rock collapse along Nepal’s border with China—swept through the Rasuwa district. Entire villages and communities were wiped out, hundreds killed, and thousands more are still missing, including many tourists. It’s an unthinkable tragedy that has unfolded with devastating consequences across parts of Nepal and neighboring Tibet.

As I exit baggage claim at Tribhuvan International Airport, one of a tiny handful of non-Nepalis on my flight from Dubai, I see a Flood Related Information & Help Desk manned by police. Outside the airport, the streets are busy, a cacophony of honking horns and motorbikes buzzing between cars, buses, and tuk-tuks as people travel around the Nepalese capital. Here, at least on the surface, things seem normal.

I’m welcomed at The Dwarika’s hotel by René Vijay Shrestha Einhaus, owner and CEO of Dwarika’s Collection. After a warm hello, the floods are the first thing we speak of; they’re in the minds and heavy hearts of everyone here. It’s a grave catastrophe that has shaken the nation. But what’s also in the minds of Nepalis is the concern that travelers to the tourism-dependent country, about to come into its peak travel season, will stop visiting.

Rescue teams and security personnel conduct helicopter search-and-rescue operations in the affected areas of Syabrubesi Bazar and Betrawoti, Rasuwa, Nepal, on September 1, 2026. NurPhoto/Getty Images

Drinking tea in the courtyard of The Dwarika’s hotel, surrounded by centuries-old Newari wood carvings, the twittering of sparrows, and the chattering of mynahs coming home to roost, feels surreally calm. As we chat, monsoon rains start pouring from the sky, a constant, thunderous downpour that hammers on the rooftops and trees, only letting up in the early hours of the following morning. It doesn’t bode well for those in the areas directly affected by the floods, or for those trying to help them.

Look at a map of Nepal and the devastated areas don’t appear all that far from the capital, but the country’s mountainous topography means that there’s no direct route between them, and the roaring rivers have no outlet into the Kathmandu Valley. The Nepal Tourism Board, and practically everyone I speak to on the ground, is keen to highlight that the devastation is concentrated in a specific area, primarily the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and parts of Dhading district. The rest of Nepal, from popular trekking areas like Everest and Annapurna, and cities like Kathmandu and Pokhara, remains unaffected and open to visitors.

KATHMANDU, Nepal — An international disaster relief cargo plane landed in Kathmandu, Nepal on Wednesday morning, delivering tons of emergency supplies to survivors of a catastrophic glacial landslide that killed hundreds and left thousands more missing.

The Boone, North Carolina-based organization Samaritan’s Purse deployed its Boeing 767 cargo aircraft loaded with more than 40 tons of aid resources. The cargo includes heavy-duty tarps, blankets, water filtration systems, hygiene kits, and solar lights.

A team of disaster response specialists accompanied the shipment to coordinate distribution alongside local partners. The deployment follows a massive glacial landslide that sent a wall of water, mud, and debris down a Nepalese river valley, destroying communities and displacing thousands of families.

“The devastation in Nepal is unimaginable,” Samaritan’s Purse President Franklin Graham said in a statement. “We’re all heartbroken to see the death toll continue to climb, and many families are still waiting for news of their missing loved ones even as they have been left with nothing but the clothes on their backs.”

The relief group previously maintained an in-country operations office in Nepal from 2015 to 2018 following a major earthquake.

Logistics crews began offloading the aircraft immediately upon arrival to expedite delivery into the hardest-hit river valley communities.

For more information and how you can help, visit samaritanspurse.org

Guests can enjoy an evening at the Michelin-recognized restaurant on Sept. 10 while helping Mercy Corps deliver urgently needed assistance to families in Nepal.

By The Georgetowner staff

A memorable dinner can make a meaningful difference on Thursday, Sept. 10, when Blue Duck Tavern invites Georgetowners and all to dine out in support of communities affected by the catastrophic flooding in Nepal.

The acclaimed restaurant at Park Hyatt Washington will donate 10 percent of its net food and beverage sales from that evening’s dinner service to Mercy Corps.

It is an opportunity to enjoy Blue Duck Tavern’s Michelin-recognized American cuisine while contributing to an important cause—simply by gathering around the table with friends, family or colleagues.

Blue Duck Tavern is known for its seasonal, locally sourced menu, open kitchen and wood-burning oven. Current dinner offerings include dry-aged beef tenderloin, pasture-raised chicken, jumbo lump crab cakes, house-made garganelli and the restaurant’s signature whole roasted duck.

Crisp-skinned fish, roasted beets and a layered pastry dessert — a sampling of Blue Duck Tavern’s seasonal, locally sourced menu at Park Hyatt Washington.

Behind the welcoming evening is an urgent need. On Aug. 26, a glacier collapse near the Nepal-China border sent a destructive surge of water, ice, rock and mud through Himalayan communities along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors.

Entire settlements were swept away, with homes, bridges, roads, health facilities and communications systems destroyed. Thousands of families have been displaced and many communities remain difficult for rescue and relief teams to reach.

Mercy Corps, which has worked in Nepal since 2005, is delivering food, clean drinking water, sanitation supplies, clothing, temporary shelter and other emergency assistance. The organization will also remain involved as affected communities begin the longer process of recovery and rebuilding.

By choosing Blue Duck Tavern for dinner on Sept. 10, guests will help support that work without adding anything extra to their checks. The restaurant itself will contribute 10 percent of its net dinner sales.

Dinner is served from 5:30 to 9:30 p.m. at Blue Duck Tavern, 1201 24th St. NW. Given the special nature of the evening, advance reservations are encouraged and may be made through Blue Duck Tavern’s website.

It is a simple and enjoyable way to help: share an exceptional meal, spend time with people you care about and allow part of the evening’s proceeds to reach families facing tremendous hardship.

More Ways to Help Nepal

Those who cannot attend the dinner—or who would like to do more—can contribute directly to organizations providing assistance in Nepal:

Mercy Corps ****: Supporting emergency food, clean water, sanitation, clothing, shelter and longer-term recovery.

UNICEF ****: Providing children and families with safe water, health and nutrition services, hygiene supplies, education assistance and protection.

American Red Cross ****: Working with the Nepal Red Cross Society to provide shelter, food, relief supplies and health services.

Save the Children ****: Supplying tents, blankets, food, hygiene kits, mosquito nets, water purifiers and child-focused assistance.

World Central Kitchen ****: Working with local partners and community kitchens to provide freshly prepared meals to survivors and emergency responders.

Project HOPE****: Mobilizing health and humanitarian assistance where the disaster has disrupted medical care, clean water and essential services.

Monetary gifts are generally the quickest and most flexible way to assist after an international disaster. Donors should contribute through an organization’s official website and check whether their employers will match charitable gifts.

अमेरिकन रेड क्रॉस **** : नेपाल रेड क्रॉस सोसाइटी के साथ मिलकर आश्रय, भोजन, राहत सामग्री एवं स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदान करना |

बच्चाक कें बचाउ ****: टेंट, कंबल, भोजन, स्वच्छता किट, मच्छरदानी, जल शुद्धिकरण आ बच्चाक पर केंद्रित सहायता कें आपूर्ति करनाय.

विश्व केंद्रीय रसोईघर ****: स्थानीय भागीदारक आ सामुदायिक रसोईघरक कें साथ मिलक क बचे वाला आ आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रियाकर्ताक कें ताजा तैयार भोजन उपलब्ध करानाय.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Donates $10 Million, Pushing Nepal Flood Relief Fund Above $65 Million - nepyork
description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Donates $10 Million, Pushing Nepal Flood Relief Fund Above $65 Million  nepyork
publisher.title: nepyork
full_article:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has donated $10 million to Nepal’s Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund to support people affected by the devastating floods in the Bhotekoshi River basin in Rasuwa district, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle said Thursday.

Wagle thanked Huang, Nvidia’s founder and chief executive, for the contribution, which he said helped push total donations to the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund above $65 million.

“On behalf of the government of Nepal, I’d like to express my sincere gratitude to Mr. Jensen Huang for donating $10 million to the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund,” Wagle said in a video message. “I hope this sizable contribution, notable by any philanthropic standard, will inspire many others to also contribute to this noble cause.”

Death Toll Rises to 1,259 as 5,053 Remain Missing

The latest situation report from Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, issued Thursday at 6 p.m., said 1,259 bodies had been recovered following the deadly floods and related disasters, while 5,053 people remained missing. Another 5,384 people were reported injured.

Rescue teams have so far rescued 12,038 people. The report said 3,926 people had been rescued by helicopter, including 3,653 Nepali citizens and 273 foreign nationals. A total of 785 air operations have been conducted, including 95 flights on Thursday.

Nepali Army personnel conduct search-and-rescue operations in flood-affected areas of Nepal. Photo: Nepali Army

A total of 304 injured people have received treatment at 18 health institutions. Of those, 200 have been discharged, 70 remain under treatment, 30 have been referred to other hospitals and four have died while receiving treatment.

The latest report said 4,521 displaced people are currently sheltering in 38 holding centers across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The centers are housing 1,141 people in Rasuwa, 3,181 in Nuwakot and 199 in Dhading.

Search-and-Rescue Operations Continue

The flood struck the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa district on Aug. 26, killing people and destroying homes, property and livelihoods. Communities in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and other districts were affected, according to an appeal issued by the Embassy of Nepal in Washington.

The government has prioritized search and rescue, relief, safe evacuation, rehabilitation and emergency response. Government agencies, local governments, security forces and other organizations have been mobilized to address immediate humanitarian needs and support longer-term recovery.

Nepali, Indian, Chinese and South Korean rescue teams continue to conduct joint search-and-rescue operations at several hydropower project sites affected by the disaster, including Rasuwagadhi, Langtang, Chilime, Upper Trishuli-1, Trishuli 3A, Trishuli 3B and Mailung Khola.

Nepali Army personnel conduct rescue operations in flood-affected areas of Nepal following the devastating Bhotekoshi floods. Photo: Nepali Army

At the Sanjen/Langtang hydropower project, rescue teams have entered about 200 meters into a tunnel and recovered two bodies or body parts. At Upper Trishuli-1, rescuers reached a blocked access area and recovered one body.

The report said 21 hospitals across various districts are currently holding unidentified bodies, while 95 identified bodies have been handed over to their families.

More Than 21,000 Security Personnel Deployed

The government has deployed 21,402 security personnel for search, rescue and relief operations. The Nepal Army has provided medical treatment to 3,206 people, while the Armed Police Force has treated another 1,874 people.

Relief supplies have been transported from Kathmandu to affected areas by 69 trucks, 38 Bolero utility vehicles and nine helicopter flights. Eleven additional trucks carrying relief supplies were dispatched Thursday.

The Armed Police Force has also transported relief materials within Nuwakot and Rasuwa through 163 air flights.

The government has provided 10 million Nepalese rupees each to Rasuwa and Nuwakot and 5 million rupees to Dhading. It has also allocated 135 million rupees for 15 affected municipalities.

Communications and Roads Slowly Recover

Telecommunications services have been restored across most of the flood-affected corridor between Dhading and the Rasuwa border. Nepal Telecom has restored 116 of its 120 mobile towers, while Ncell has restored 75 of its 78 towers.

Some areas, including Timure, Chilime Khola and Trishuli 3B for Nepal Telecom and Timure, Trishuli and Uttargaya-1 for Ncell, still lack mobile service. The government is also preparing to deploy additional low-Earth-orbit satellite terminals in affected areas.

Road access remains a major challenge. Traffic is completely obstructed at Krishnabhir along the Mugling-Malekhu section of the Prithvi Highway, while authorities are working to excavate the hillside and construct a new road.

Three alternative routes connecting Kathmandu through Abukhaireni, Dhadingbesi and Benighat have been identified.

The 55-meter Devighat Bridge over the Tadi River was washed away, and the Nepal Army has begun transporting materials from Gajuri for construction of a Bailey bridge.

On the Bidur-Betrawati road, 7.5 kilometers of a 10-kilometer section has been cleared, while the remaining 2.5 kilometers was completely washed away.

Trishuli in Nuwakot after flooding in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa, Nepal. Photo: Dipendra Dhungana/NepYork

Government Appeals for Donations

The Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers has appealed to individuals, organizations, businesses, private-sector entities and well-wishers in Nepal and abroad to contribute to the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund.

The government said contributions will support rescue operations, relief assistance, safe evacuation and the long-term rehabilitation of people affected by the Bhotekoshi flood.

In a separate appeal, the Embassy of Nepal in Washington urged Nepalis in the United States and in countries under its concurrent accreditation — Mexico, Costa Rica, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras, Panama, Guatemala and The Bahamas — to support the relief effort.

The embassy also called on Nepali diaspora groups, businesses, philanthropists, and U.S. and international organizations to contribute according to their capacity.

The embassy urged donors to use official channels only and to verify bank account names, QR codes and other payment details to help ensure that donations are handled securely and transparently and reach their intended purpose.

वित्त मंत्री स्वर्णिम वागले बृहस्पतिदिन कहलनि जे, रसुवा जिलाक भोटेकोशी नदी बेसिन मे आयल विनाशकारी बाढ़ि सं प्रभावित लोकक सहायता लेल नेपालक प्रधानमंत्री आपदा राहत कोष मे एक करोड़ डॉलर के दान देलनि अछि।

वागले न॑ एनवीडिया केरऽ संस्थापक आरू मुख्य कार्यकारी हुआंग क॑ ई योगदान लेली धन्यवाद देलकै, जेकरा स॑ हुनकऽ कहना छै कि प्रधानमंत्री आपदा राहत कोष म॑ कुल दान क॑ ६.५ करोड़ डॉलर स॑ ऊपर बढ़ाबै म॑ मदद मिललै ।

वागले न॑ वीडियो संदेश म॑ कहलकै कि हम्में नेपाल सरकार के तरफ स॑ श्री जेन्सन हुआंग क॑ प्रधानमंत्री आपदा राहत कोष म॑ एक करोड़ डॉलर के दान दै लेली हार्दिक आभार व्यक्त करना चाहै छियै । “हमरा आशा छै कि कोनो भी परोपकारी मानक स॑ उल्लेखनीय ई काफी योगदान, बहुत लोगऽ क॑ भी ई उदात्त काज म॑ योगदान दै लेली प्रेरित करतै।”

5053 लोग लापता रहला के कारण मृतक के संख्या बढ़ि क 1259 भ गेल

नेपालक राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम न्यूनीकरण आ प्रबंधन प्राधिकरणक नवीनतम स्थिति रिपोर्ट बृहस्पतिदिन साँझ ६ बजे जारी कएल गेल अछि जे घातक बाढ़ि आ एहि सँ जुड़ल आपदाक बाद १,२५९ शव बरामद भेल अछि, जखन कि ५,०५३ गोटे लापता अछि । आओर 5384 लोक घायल हेबाक सूचना अछि।

अखन नेपयोर्क कें मुफ्त सदस्यता लिअ, अहां यू.एस.वीजा, ग्रीन कार्ड, आ सब आप्रवासन समाचारक कें कोनों अपडेट कें संग-संग आवास, कर, स्वास्थ्य देखभाल, आ बहुत किछु पर आवश्यक जानकारी आ संसाधनक कें सेहो छूटि नहिं जायब. एकरा सब के सीधा अपन इनबॉक्स में पहुंचा दियौ। ईमेल पता एतय दर्ज करू... सब्सक्राइब करय लेल एतय क्लिक करू

बचाव दल एखन धरि 12,038 लोक के बचा चुकल अछि। रिपोर्टमे कहल गेल अछि जे हेलीकॉप्टरसँ ३,९२६ गोटेके उद्धार कएल गेल अछि, जाहिमे ३,६५३ नेपाली नागरिक आ २७३ विदेशी नागरिक रहल अछि । बृहस्पतिदिन ९५ उड्डाण सहित कुल ७८५ हवाई परिचालन भेल अछि ।

नेपालके बाढ़ प्रभावित क्षेत्रमे नेपाली सेनाके जवानसब खोजी-बचाव कार्यवाही करैत अछि । फोटो : नेपाली सेना

कुल 304 घायल लोक के 18 स्वास्थ्य संस्थान मे इलाज कराओल गेल अछि। ओहि मे स 200 गोटे कए डिस्चार्ज क देल गेल अछि, 70 गोटे कए इलाज मे अछि, 30 गोटे कए अन्य अस्पताल मे रेफर कैल गेल अछि आ चारि गोटे कए इलाज क दौरान मौत भ गेल अछि।

ताजा रिपोर्ट मे कहल गेल अछि जे एखन 4521 विस्थापित लोक रसुवा, नुवाकोट आ धडिंग भरि मे 38 होल्डिंग सेंटर मे आश्रय मे छथि। केन्द्रमे रसुवामे १,१४१, नुवाकोटमे ३,१८१ आ धादिङमे १९९१ गोटेके आवास रहल अछि ।

खोज-बचाव अभियान जारी अछि

रसुवा जिला के भोटेकोशी नदी मे 26 अगस्त के बाढ़ि मे लोक के मौत भ गेल छल आओर घर, संपत्ति आओर रोजी-रोटी के तबाह भ गेल छल. रसुवा, नुवाकोट, धाडिंग, गोरखा आदि जिलाक समुदाय प्रभावित भेल वाशिंगटनमे नेपालक दूतावाससँ जारी अपीलमे जानकारी देल गेल अछि ।

सरकार खोज आ बचाव, राहत, सुरक्षित निकासी, पुनर्वास आ आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया के प्राथमिकता देलक अछि। तत्काल मानवीय जरूरतक कें पूरा करय आ दीर्घकालिक वसूली कें समर्थन कें लेल सरकारी एजेंसी, स्थानीय सरकार, सुरक्षा बल आ अन्य संगठनक कें जुटान कैल गेल छै.

आपदासँ प्रभावित अनेक जलविद्युत परियोजना स्थलमे नेपाली, भारतीय, चीनी आ दक्षिण कोरियाके बचाव दल संयुक्त रूपसँ खोज-बचाव अभियान जारी रखने अछि, जाहिमे रसुवागाढी, लंगटांग, चिलीमे, अपर त्रिशुली-१, त्रिशुली ३ए, त्रिशुली ३ बी आ मैलुंग खोला शामिल अछि ।

भोटेकोशीके विनाशकारी बाढिक बाद नेपालके बाढ़ प्रभावित क्षेत्रमे नेपाली सेनाके जवान उद्धार कार्यवाही करैत अछि । फोटो : नेपाली सेना

संजेन/लंगटांग जलविद्युत परियोजना मे बचाव दल करीब 200 मीटर दूर एकटा सुरंग मे घुसि कए दूटा लाश या शरीर क अंग बरामद केलक अछि। अपर त्रिशुली-१ मे बचावकर्मी अवरुद्ध पहुँच क्षेत्र मे पहुँचि एकटा लाश बरामद केलक।

रिपोर्ट मे कहल गेल अछि जे विभिन्न जिलाक 21 अस्पताल मे एखन अज्ञात लाश राखल गेल अछि, जखन कि 95 चिन्हित लाश परिवार के सौंपल गेल अछि।

21 हजार स बेसी सुरक्षा कर्मी तैनात

सरकार खोज, बचाव आ राहत कार्य मे २१,४०२ सुरक्षाकर्मी तैनात केने अछि । नेपाली सेना ३,२०६ गोटेके चिकित्सा उपचार प्रदान केने अछि, ओतहि सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल १,८७४ गोटेके उपचार केने अछि ।

काठमांडू सँ ६९ ट्रक, ३८ बोलेरो उपयोगिता वाहन आ ९ हेलीकॉप्टर उड्डाण सँ प्रभावित क्षेत्र मे राहत सामग्री पहुँचाओल गेल अछि । गुरुवार कए राहत सामग्री ल कए एगारहटा अतिरिक्त ट्रक भेजल गेल।

सशस्त्र पुलिस बल 163 हवाई उड़ान के माध्यम सं नुवाकोट आ रसुवा के भीतर राहत सामग्री के परिवहन सेहो केने अछि.

सरकार रसुवा आ नुवाकोट के एक-एक करोड़ नेपाली रुपैया आ धडिंग के ५० लाख रुपैया उपलब्ध करौलक अछि । संगहि 15 प्रभावित नगरपालिका लेल 13.5 करोड़ रुपया आवंटित केलक अछि।

संचार आ सड़क धीरे-धीरे ठीक भ रहल अछि

धादिङ आ रसुवा सीमाक बीच बाढ़ि प्रभावित अधिकांश गलियारा मे दूरसंचार सेवा बहाल कएल गेल अछि । नेपाल दूरसंचार अपन १२० मोबाइल टावर मे सँ ११६ टावर बहाली केलक अछि, जखन कि एनसेल अपन ७८ टावर मे सँ ७५ टावर के जीर्णोद्धार केलक अछि ।

नेपाल दूरसंचारके लेल तैमुरे, चिलिमे खोला आ त्रिशुली ३बी आ एनसेलके लेल तिमुरे, त्रिशुली आ उत्तरगया-१ सहित किछु क्षेत्रमे अखनो मोबाइल सेवाक अभाव अछि । सरकार प्रभावित क्षेत्र मँ अतिरिक्त कम पृथ्वी कक्षा वाला उपग्रह टर्मिनल तैनात करै के तैयारी भी करी रहलौ छै ।

सड़क पर पहुंच एकटा पैघ चुनौती बनल अछि। पृथ्वी राजमार्ग के मुगलिंग-मालेखु खंड के किनारे कृष्णाभिर में यातायात पूर्ण रूप स बाधित अछि, जखन कि अधिकारी पहाड़ी ढाल के खुदाई आ नव सड़क के निर्माण के काज क रहल छथि।

अबुखैरेनी, धादिङबेसी आ बेनिघाट होइत काठमाण्डौकेँ जोड़यवला तीनटा वैकल्पिक मार्गक पहिचान कएल गेल अछि ।

ताडी नदी पर बनल 55 मीटर लंबा देवीघाट पुल बहल गेल, आ नेपाली सेना बेली पुल बनेबा लेल गजुरी स सामग्री परिवहन शुरू क देलक अछि।

बिदुर-बेतरावती सड़क पर 10 किलोमीटर के 7.5 किलोमीटर के खंड साफ भ गेल अछि, जखन कि शेष 2.5 किलोमीटर पूरा तरह सं बहल गेल अछि.

नेपाल के रसुवा के भोटेकोशी नदी में बाढ़ के बाद नुवाकोट के त्रिशुली। फोटो : दिपेन्द्र ढुंगाना/नेपयोर्क

चंदा के लिये सरकारी अपील

प्रधानमन्त्री आ मन्त्रिपरिषद्के कार्यालय नेपाल आ विदेशमे रहल व्यक्ति, संस्था, व्यवसायी, निजी क्षेत्रके संस्था आ शुभचिन्तकसबसँ प्रधानमन्त्री आपदा राहत कोषमे योगदान देबाक अपील केने अछि ।

सरकार के कहनाय छनि जे एहि योगदान सं बचाव अभियान, राहत सहायता, सुरक्षित निकासी आओर भोटेकोशी बाढ़ि सं प्रभावित लोक के दीर्घकालीन पुनर्वास मे मदद मिलत.

वाशिंगटन मँ नेपाल केरौ दूतावास नँ एगो अलग अपील मँ अमेरिका आरू ओकरौ समवर्ती मान्यता के तहत देशौ मँ नेपाली सिनी स॑ आग्रह करलकै – मेक्सिको, कोस्टा रिका, बेलीज, एल साल्वाडोर, होन्डुरस, पनामा, ग्वाटेमाला आरू द बहामास — कि हुनी राहत प्रयास के समर्थन करै ।

दूतावास नेपाली प्रवासी समूह, व्यवसायी, परोपकारी, आ अमेरिकी आ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संगठन सब स सेहो अपन क्षमता के अनुसार योगदान देबाक आह्वान केलक अछि ।

दूतावास न॑ दाता सब स॑ आग्रह करलकै कि वू केवल आधिकारिक चैनल के इस्तेमाल करै आरू बैंक खाता के नाम, क्यूआर कोड आरू अन्य भुगतान विवरण के सत्यापन करै ताकि ई सुनिश्चित करै म॑ मदद मिल॑ सक॑ कि दान क॑ सुरक्षित आरू पारदर्शी तरीका स॑ संभाललऽ जाय आरू ओकरऽ इच्छित उद्देश्य तलक पहुँचै ।

Drones, dogs, and data

A South Korean team of rescue workers equipped with drones, rescue dogs, acoustic equipment, video and thermal imaging machinery set up base in Batar, near the tunnel of the Upper Trishuli -1 hydropower plant, where nine South Korean workers went missing.

An army officer involved in the search-and-rescue operation said the search was continuing with experts from India, South Korea and China, and that “The search-and-rescue operation will continue as long as there is any hope of finding survivors.” Egyptian Gazette

Phanindra Paudel, an official at Nepal’s National Emergency Operation Centre, said, “People have lost everything. They don’t have citizenship IDs or passports,” as authorities worked to restore routines and focus on getting children into makeshift schools.

UNICEF said that more than a week after the flood, at least 22,000 children urgently need safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene support, while authorities considered whether children could be taught in holding centres.

An Australian medical student whose partner went missing near the Nepal-China border urged tech companies to share tracking data to narrow search areas for rescue teams, and Reuters reported Australia pledged additional support and said it would also share telecommunications data with Nepali authorities.

ड्रोन, कुत्ता, आ डाटा

ड्रोन, बचाव कुत्ता, ध्वनिक उपकरण, वीडियो आरू थर्मल इमेजिंग मशीनरी स॑ लैस बचावकर्मी केरऽ दक्षिण कोरियाई टीम न॑ ऊपरी त्रिशुली -१ जलविद्युत संयंत्र केरऽ सुरंग के पास बतार म॑ अड्डा बनैलकै, जहां दक्षिण कोरिया केरऽ नौ मजदूर लापता होय गेलै ।

खोज-बचाव अभियान स॑ जुड़लऽ एगो सेना अधिकारी न॑ कहलकै कि भारत, दक्षिण कोरिया आरू चीन केरऽ विशेषज्ञऽ के साथ खोज जारी छै, आरू “जब तलक खोज-बचाव अभियान तब तलक जारी रहतै जब॑ तलक कि बची गेलऽ लोगऽ के खोज के कोय उम्मीद नै रहतै।” मिस्र के राजपत्र

नेपाल के राष्ट्रीय आपातकालीन संचालन केंद्र के अधिकारी फनींद्र पौडेल कहलनि जे, लोक सब किछु गंवा देलक अछि, हुनका लग नागरिकता आईडी या पासपोर्ट नहि अछि, कियाक त अधिकारी दिनचर्या के बहाल करय आ बच्चा के अस्थायी स्कूल में भर्ती करय पर ध्यान केंद्रित केलक।

यूनिसेफ नँ कहलकै कि बाढ़ के एक सप्ताह स॑ भी अधिक समय बाद कम स॑ कम २२ हजार बच्चा सिनी क॑ सुरक्षित पेयजल, स्वच्छता आरू स्वच्छता के सहायता के तत्काल जरूरत छै, जबकि अधिकारियऽ न॑ ई बात प॑ विचार करलकै कि की बच्चा सिनी क॑ होल्डिंग सेंटर म॑ पढ़ायलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै ।

एक ऑस्ट्रेलियाई मेडिकल छात्र, जेकरऽ साथी नेपाल-चीन सीमा के पास लापता होय गेलऽ छेलै, न॑ टेक कंपनी सिनी स॑ आग्रह करलकै कि वू बचाव टीम लेली खोज क्षेत्र क॑ संकीर्ण करै लेली ट्रैकिंग डाटा साझा करै, आरू रायटर न॑ रिपोर्ट करलकै कि ऑस्ट्रेलिया न॑ अतिरिक्त सहायता के वादा करलकै आरू कहलकै कि वू नेपाली अधिकारियऽ के साथ दूरसंचार डाटा भी साझा करतै ।
